name: Pellucid BioSeal Class-3 Geneware Theater Suit
description:
A full-body cleanroom suit in translucent pearl-white, the outer layer a smooth electrostatically-dissipative film over a sealed microfiber inner shell. The hood is integrated with a clear polycarbonate face shield and a filtered-air collar port. All seams are RF-welded. The suit comes in sealed single-use packaging but is built for up to thirty decontamination cycles before disposal rating drops.

Designed for geneware surgical theaters and high-biosafety genomics labs at Tier 4 facilities. The translucency is functional — supervisors can observe limb positioning and hand placement through the suit during delicate procedures. A fine silver-thread grid woven into the outer film provides passive ESD protection for sensitive genomic equipment.
functionality: ISO Class 3 cleanroom rated. ESD protection via silver-thread grid. Filtered-air collar port compatible with standard lab air supply lines. Hood-integrated face shield with anti-fog inner coating. Rated for 30 decontamination cycles. Translucent outer layer for supervisor observation.
what_it_says: You operate in controlled environments where a single contamination event costs millions and possibly someone's life.
price_range: Φ 340–Φ 680 per unit (bulk lab contract pricing varies)
story_hooks: A Class-3 suit from a geneware theater was found outside the facility with trace biologics inside that don't match any patient or staff DNA on record.
A researcher has been wearing the same suit past its 30-cycle disposal rating for months — she claims the suit's translucency has started showing something that isn't her body underneath.
A shipment of Pellucid suits to a black-market geneware clinic was intercepted — but only half the shipment was recovered.

physical_description.visual_profile: A ethereal, ghost-like full-body silhouette in translucent pearl-white. The suit creates a cocoon effect, obscuring the wearer's natural form while maintaining visibility of movement and positioning. The integrated hood and clear polycarbonate face shield give an alien, clinical appearance — part medical worker, part containment protocol.
physical_description.fit: Precisely tailored yet allowing freedom of movement for precise surgical gestures. Not baggy, but not compression-tight — a functional middle ground that prioritizes dexterity and observable limb placement. Cuffed wrists and ankles create secure seals.
physical_description.primary_material: Electrostatically-dissipative translucent polymer film layered over sealed microfiber base. The outer layer is smooth and slightly glossy; the inner microfiber provides structural integrity and comfort against skin.
physical_description.texture: Outer surface: slick, almost frictionless polymer film with a faint sheen. Inner surface: soft microfiber with subtle texture. Fine silver-thread grid creates a barely-perceptible raised pattern across the entire suit — visible up close but seamless from distance.
physical_description.color_scheme: Translucent pearl-white with an underlying slight iridescence. The silver-thread ESD grid appears as a faint geometric web, most visible at seams and under strong lighting. The polycarbonate face shield is completely clear with slight amber tinting at edges.
physical_description.closures: RF-welded seams throughout — no traditional closures. Full-body entry via a rear torso RF-weld seam (opened during doffing procedures). Integrated collar port accepts filtered-air tubing via friction-fit connection. No zippers, buckles, or exposed fasteners.
distinctive_features: Integrated clear polycarbonate face shield molded into hood
Filtered-air collar port with friction-fit tubing connector
Silver-thread ESD grid woven into outer film for equipment protection
RF-welded seams throughout for complete environmental seal
Translucency allows supervisor observation of hand and limb positioning
Sealed single-use packaging but rated for up to 30 decontamination cycles
Fine microfiber inner shell for comfort during extended wear
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional. Expensive enough to signal institutional access and technical credibility, but utilitarian rather than luxury. The single-use packaging and decontamination cycle rating indicate mid-tier facility deployment.
physical_description.cultural_context: Marks the wearer as a geneware technician, genomics researcher, or surgical theater specialist. Signals institutional authority, sterile protocol adherence, and access to sensitive biotech facilities. The suit creates psychological distance — a barrier between the wearer's humanity and the sterile work environment.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when first worn, with visible creasing from sealed packaging. After 5-10 cycles: minor surface scuffing, slight cloudiness at high-flex points (elbows, knees), but still functional. By cycle 25-30: accumulating micro-abrasions, clouding at seams, but seal integrity maintained.
